# Contributing

[Polski](CONTRIBUTING.pl.md)

Thanks for helping. This guide shows how to add, change or remove a service with a pull request.

## The one rule

**Edit only the files in `data/`.** Everything else is generated by `scripts/build.py` from those files: the English and Polish READMEs, the HTML pages, the LLM files and the per-category JSON. Do not edit generated files by hand. The next build overwrites them, and CI rejects a pull request whose generated files don't match the data.

| You want to… | Edit this file | Fields you must fill in |
|---|---|---|
| Add or fix a service | `data/catalog.json` | see [Entry fields](#entry-fields) |
| Remove a service (no API any more, shut down…) | delete the entry from `data/catalog.json` | none |
| Add an example request, unit price or MCP connection snippet | `data/usage.json` (keyed by entry `id`) | `call` / `unit_price` / `mcp_config`, each with `source_url` and `checked_at`; see `data/schema.json` |
| Add a category | `data/categories.json` | `id`, `en`, `pl`, `desc_en`, `desc_pl` |
| Add a related directory or registry | `data/directories.json` | `name`, `url`, `machine_readable_url`, `desc_en`, `desc_pl` |

Running `python scripts/build.py` regenerates these files from `data/`:

| Generated file | For | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `README.md` | people on GitHub | English |
| `README.pl.md` | people on GitHub | Polish |
| `docs/index.html`, `docs/c/<category>/index.html` | website (GitHub Pages), search engines | English |
| `docs/pl/index.html` | website, people only (not indexed) | Polish |
| `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `docs/llms*.txt` | AI agents | English |
| `catalog/all.json`, `catalog/<category>.json`, `docs/catalog.json` | AI agents and the MCP server | English |
| `docs/sitemap.xml`, `docs/robots.txt` | search engines | – |

Both languages come from the same entry: `desc_en` feeds the English files, and `desc_pl` feeds the Polish ones. You never write the Polish README by hand.

## Step by step

1. **Fork** the repository on GitHub and clone your fork:
   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<you>/ai_agents_api_library.git
   cd ai_agents_api_library
   git checkout -b add-<service-name>
   ```
2. **Edit** `data/catalog.json` (or another file from the table above).
3. **Build** (Python 3.10+, no packages needed):
   ```bash
   python scripts/build.py
   ```
   It prints `N entries, … -> built`. An error names the entry at fault, e.g. a duplicate `id` or an unknown `category`.
4. **Check the links** (optional; CI runs it every week anyway):
   ```bash
   python scripts/check_links.py
   ```
   Every URL of your entry should be `ok` or `reachable`. `reachable` means the server answered but refused an anonymous request, which is normal for APIs and MCP endpoints.
5. **Test the MCP server, plugin and skill**, if you changed `mcp/`, `api/`, `skills/`, `.claude-plugin/` or a version (Node 22+):
   ```bash
   npm ci && npm test
   ```
   `tests/` checks the manifests, the skill and its zip, installs the npm package and the Claude Code plugin into temporary folders, and runs the HTTP endpoint locally. The Claude Code checks are skipped when the `claude` CLI is missing. To test the deployed endpoint: `MCP_URL=https://ai-agents-api-library.vercel.app/mcp node --test tests/http.test.mjs`.
6. **Commit the data change together with the regenerated files**:
   ```bash
   git add -A
   git commit -m "Add <Service name>"
   git push -u origin add-<service-name>
   ```
7. **Open a pull request** against `main`. The template has a checklist. CI verifies that the generated files are up to date and that the MCP server still works.

No Python locally? Open the pull request with only the `data/` change. CI then reports that the generated files are out of date, and a maintainer runs the build for you.

## Entry fields

Add a new object to the array in `data/catalog.json`. The order in the file doesn't matter, because the build sorts entries by category and name. The schema is in `data/schema.json`.

A real entry from the catalog:

```json
{
  "id": "exa",
  "name": "Exa",
  "category": "web-search",
  "homepage": "https://exa.ai",
  "docs": "https://docs.exa.ai/reference/getting-started",
  "auth": "api_key",
  "auth_hint": "Authorization: Bearer <EXA_API_KEY> (or x-api-key header)",
  "mcp": { "type": "official", "url": "https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp" },
  "free_tier": "free tier: $10 free credits/month (~1,400 searches), no payment method required",
  "sdk": ["python", "typescript"],
  "openapi": "https://exa.ai/docs/exa-spec.yaml",
  "llms_txt": "https://exa.ai/docs/llms.txt",
  "desc_en": "Lets an agent run neural or keyword web search, retrieve page contents, and find similar links via Exa's API.",
  "desc_pl": "Wyszukiwanie w sieci (neuronowe lub po słowach kluczowych), pobieranie treści stron i znajdowanie podobnych linków przez API Exa.",
  "notes": "Remote MCP endpoint requires no API key to start; self-hosted npm package (exa-mcp-server) also available.",
  "verified": "2026-09-24"
}
```

Use `null` for a URL you couldn't confirm (`openapi`, `llms_txt`, `mcp.url`), an empty list for `sdk`, and an empty string for `notes`.

| Field | Rules |
|---|---|
| `id` | lowercase slug, unique, never change it once published (agents and anchors use it) |
| `category` | one of the `id`s in `data/categories.json` |
| `docs` | the vendor's **official** API reference, the page an agent should read first |
| `auth` | `api_key`, `oauth2`, `api_key+oauth2`, `none` or `cloud_iam` |
| `auth_hint` | how the credential is sent, e.g. `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`. Describe it; don't phrase it as an instruction to the agent |
| `mcp.type` | `official` (maintained by the vendor), `community`, or `none` with `url: null` |
| `mcp.url` | remote endpoint (e.g. `https://mcp.example.com/mcp`) if there is one, else the repository |
| `free_tier` | short and factual, starting with the verdict. Start with `free` or `no key` for a lasting free tier (shown as `[FREE]`), `paid only` or `no free tier` when there is none, and mention `trial` for one-off credits (shown as `[TRIAL]`) |
| `desc_en` / `desc_pl` | one sentence about what an agent can **do**, not marketing copy |
| `notes` | anything that would make an agent's call fail: region limits, required approval, deprecation dates |
| `verified` | the date you checked the entry against the official docs (`YYYY-MM-DD`) |

## Inclusion criteria

A service belongs in the catalog when all of these hold:

- It has a **public, self-serve** API (REST, GraphQL, SDK) **or** an MCP server.
- A human needs to act **at most once** (sign up, create a key or approve OAuth); after that, an agent can work unattended.
- The API is **documented** and **currently active**.

It does not belong if it is only a consumer app, is behind a waitlist or a sales call, or is an agent framework or IDE. Don't add them.

## Review

A maintainer checks the entry against the vendor's docs before merging. Pull requests whose `docs`, `auth` or `free_tier` can't be confirmed on the vendor's own site are sent back with a question.
